attributes.source_locator: Supplementary Information, Model Architecture (PDF pages 4-7) and Supplementary Table 10 (PDF page 27)
attributes.value: GPN-Star is an encoder-only masked language model whose encoder blocks apply sequence-wise self-attention, phylogeny-informed cross-attention and a feed-forward network. Supplementary Table 10 gives the three sizes as 25M, 85M and 200M parameters with 8, 12 and 16 encoder blocks, hidden dimension 512, 768 and 1024, intermediate size 2048, 3072 and 4096, 4, 6 and 8 self-attention heads, the same number of cross-attention heads, attention head dimension 64 and dropout rate 0.1 throughout.

attributes.source_locator: Supplementary Information, Evaluation Benchmarks, Homo sapiens, Datasets (PDF pages 11-12)
attributes.value: The OMIM benchmark uses the processed Mendelian traits dataset from TraitGym and the non-coding fine-mapping benchmark uses the processed complex traits dataset from TraitGym, both with nine controls matched per positive on chromosome, molecular consequence and distance to the transcription start site, and for complex traits also on LD score and minor allele frequency. HGMD was processed in the same way as the TraitGym Mendelian traits dataset. Coding fine-mapped variants come from the same fine-mapping source but are matched on minor allele frequency only. The paper does not name a TraitGym revision.

attributes.source_locator: Supplementary Information, 'Key differences between GPN-MSA and GPN-Star' (PDF page 2)
attributes.value: GPN-Star differs from GPN-MSA in three ways the authors name: it masks and predicts nucleotides across many species rather than the human genome alone; it encodes phylogenetic relationships explicitly through its attention modules; and it accepts alignments of any composition and size, so it does not need the manual species curation that GPN-MSA required, such as excluding species closely related to human.

attributes.value: Among the top 0.1% most constrained common variants by GPN-Star (P), missense variants are the largest class at 33% and 170-fold enriched, followed by variants in distal enhancer-like regions at 26% and 2.4-fold enriched and their flanks at 8% and 0.35-fold depleted. attributes.source_locator: Supplementary Information, Supplementary Table 1 (PDF page 21) and Training Data (PDF pages 7-8)
attributes.value: The three human models are trained on whole-genome alignments at three timescales: multiz100way (100 vertebrates), cactus447way restricted to 447 mammals, and cactus447way restricted to 243 primates, all on hg38. Chromosomes 1-20, X and Y are training data, chromosome 21 is validation and chromosome 22 is a held-out test chromosome. Five further models are trained for Mus musculus (mm39, multiz35way), Gallus gallus (galGal6, multiz77way), Drosophila melanogaster (dm6, multiz124way), Caenorhabditis elegans (ce11, multiz135way) and Arabidopsis thaliana (tair10, multiz18way).

name: ProteinGym v0.1 human deep mutational scanning assays in genomic coordinates (GPN-Star paper)

denominator.note: Variant counts are not printed for this dataset

review.method_note: Independent review pass of 2026-11-16. All four pinned artifacts were re-retrieved. The Nature article PDF, the Supplementary Information PDF and the Hugging Face collection API JSON each hashed to the value on their source record. The bioRxiv PDF did not and cannot: two downloads minutes apart gave b3e4d729d3363c16fb6b6cb99e4e18ffadb01b48614dba910480fb96f42b3d73 and 47f87f72baf93793177d3e40f70f43f03ac5d3050bbc5244f655e92041c7db4a, differing from each other in 34 bytes, all of them download-time stamps (XMP ModifyDate and MetadataDate, the xmpMM DocumentID and InstanceID, the document /ModDate and the second element of the trailer /ID); the page count, the CreationDate of 2025-09-21 and the pdftotext -layout text layer are identical across downloads. No value in this batch comes from the preprint. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly: 12 in_cell, 44 in_row, 16 locator_not_parsed, no not_in_row, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row (value-check.tsv). All 72 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build.py. Supplementary Table 3 is printed rotated, so that script reads the page's word bounding boxes rather than a text dump: it recovers the seven column bands from the header words' y extents, pairing each 'Finemapped' header with whichever of 'coding' and 'non-coding' overlaps it, clusters the body words into eight row bands by x centre, and places every numeric token in the cell whose column centre is nearest, rejecting any token that is more than 45 per cent of a column pitch from its nearest column or less than 25 per cent of a pitch clear of the runner-up. Column order is therefore a measured property of the page and not an assumption, which is the check extract/build.py could not make: it asserted the column order positionally. Results are matched to cells through each source_locator's text, not through record IDs. Fig. 4b's 12 bar labels were required to be the first number printed after their series label on the same line, and the four rare variant counts were matched against the two sentences that print them, with the capture position fixing which count belongs to DeepRVAT with GPN-Star annotations and which to the original method. Result: 68 in cell, 4 in sentence, 0 failures (review/value-check-independent.tsv). Two negative controls confirm the checker is a cell check and not a row check: exchanging two ClinVar values between rows and moving a Fig. 4b label onto another series both fail (review/control-swap.tsv), and shifting a value into a neighbouring column of its own row fails and names the column that actually holds it, including across the Finemapped coding / OMIM and Finemapped coding / Finemapped non-coding boundaries (review/control-shift.tsv). Independently of both scripts, all 56 cells of Supplementary Table 3 and all 12 Fig. 4b labels were transcribed by hand from the pages rendered at 190 dpi with pdftoppm, into review/manual-transcription.tsv, and compared by review/cmp_manual.py: 68 values, 0 problems. That hand pass is what settles the column assignment the repository checker could only place at row level. The 12 descriptive claims were read against the pinned PDFs and the collection JSON.
review.note: Construction, controls and release were checked against the Evaluation Benchmarks bullet the locator names.
review.reviewer_note: Claude review agent (independent of the extractor); no human review claimed. Values were checked against the pinned artifacts; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

No value in this batch comes from the preprint. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly: 12 in_cell, 44 in_row, 16 locator_not_parsed, no not_in_row, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row (value-check.tsv).
